note: The major pentatonic as the major scale less two notes (scales:2): C major on a staff with the 4th and 7th faded and the two half steps they make tapped from the text, then tunes made up over a drone on G major pentatonic, the second key, with a line on what stays the same. The keys are fixed (C, then G a 5th up), so there are no moves.

exercise.title: Major pentatonic: five notes of the major scale
exercise.why: The major pentatonic is the major scale without its 4th and 7th, the two notes a half step from a neighbour, so no two of its five notes are a half step apart and almost any order of them makes a tune.

cells.text:
The staff below shows the C major scale with two notes faded, the 4th and the 7th. Tap up the five notes that are left, from {{1}} to the next {{1}}: that is the C major pentatonic scale.
Then tap {{3}} and {{4}}, and {{7}} and {{1}}, to hear the two half steps the pentatonic scale does without.
Practice until you can say which notes are faded before you look.

Press Play below to start the drone on G. The staff under it holds the G major pentatonic scale: the same five notes of the scale, from a new home note. Make up short tunes by tapping, with leaps as well as steps, and end each one on a ringed {{1}}.
In G the notes are new, and the two gaps are still where the 4th and the 7th would be.
